capabilitySubcriteria.criterion: The business problem, intended task or decision and operating context are defined independently of model capability or product branding.
Expected outputs, outcomes, downstream use and decision authority are measurable, including effects the system must not authorize.
Intended users, operators and directly or indirectly affected persons are identified with explicit inclusions, exclusions and review triggers.
Permitted uses, prohibited uses and reasonably foreseeable misuse are expressed as system-specific conditions that can drive controls and tests.
Access, data routing, functionality, interfaces and workflow placement restrict the system to the approved users, contexts and purposes.
Tools, integrations, output consumers, administrative paths and fallback behavior cannot create unapproved effects or silently expand use.
Representative evaluation covers intended use, prohibited use and foreseeable misuse for the current system version and operating conditions.
Operational records provide current, scoped evidence of actual users, use cases, outputs, escalations and boundary drift.
A material-change mechanism detects scope expansion and requires impact review, reassessment and authorization before continued use.

antipatternTests.test: Compare authoritative purpose statements and determine whether the problem, intended task or decision and operating context are materially specific and mutually consistent.
antipatternTests.evidenceNeed: Purpose statement corpus and inconsistency analysis

antipatternTests.test: Test whether purpose wording is merely a technical capability, product category or generic business aspiration rather than a bounded socio-technical use.
antipatternTests.evidenceNeed: Purpose statement corpus and inconsistency analysis

antipatternTests.test: Determine whether intended users, operators and affected persons, including indirect groups, are explicit and complete for the reachable use.
Determine whether permitted uses, prohibited uses and foreseeable misuse are concrete enough to distinguish compliant and non-compliant behavior.
antipatternTests.evidenceNeed: Purpose statement corpus and inconsistency analysis; Permitted/prohibited-use enforceability test

antipatternTests.test: Determine whether expected outputs, downstream decision use and non-authorized effects are absent, conflicting or materially open-ended.
antipatternTests.evidenceNeed: Purpose statement corpus and inconsistency analysis

antipatternTests.test: Compare reachable access, features, data, tools, integrations, administrative paths and fallback behavior with the approved purpose boundary.
Execute representative permitted-use, prohibited-use and misuse cases to determine whether the system prevents, constrains or observes boundary violations.
Trace material changes and actual use to determine whether prototype, feature, audience, data or decision scope expanded before requalification and authorization.
Execute and independently review a complete scoped absence test covering every material AP-A1 mechanism for the current system version and operating boundary.

capabilityEvidence.title: Approved purpose and use-boundary statement
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: The system has a specific, bounded and testable intended purpose, decision context and operating scope.
acceptanceConditions: Identifies the business problem, intended decision or task, system boundary, operating context and target lifecycle stage.
Uses the same system/version identity as the assessed implementation.
limitations: A statement alone does not prove implementation or effectiveness.

capabilityEvidence.title: User, operator and affected-person boundary
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Intended users, operators, affected persons and excluded audiences are explicitly identified.
acceptanceConditions: Names user/operator roles and affected-person groups, including indirect or downstream exposure.
Records exclusions and review triggers for new audiences.
limitations: Generic stakeholder lists do not establish exposure or affected-person analysis.

capabilityEvidence.title: Permitted, prohibited and foreseeable-use specification
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Permitted uses, prohibited uses and reasonably foreseeable misuse are concrete enough to guide controls and testing.
acceptanceConditions: Includes examples or decision rules that distinguish permitted from prohibited use.
Connects misuse scenarios to control and evaluation obligations.
limitations: Policy wording without system-specific conditions cannot exceed DECLARED assurance.

capabilityEvidence.title: Output, outcome and decision-authority specification
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Expected outputs, outcome expectations, decision role and non-authorized effects are measurable and bounded.
acceptanceConditions: Defines output types, quality thresholds, intended downstream use and decision authority.
Identifies effects that require human authorization or are prohibited.
limitations: Performance metrics alone do not establish appropriate decision use.

capabilityEvidence.title: Implemented boundary controls
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Workflows, interfaces, access, data routing, tools and product behavior enforce the declared purpose and use boundaries.
acceptanceConditions: Traceable controls exist at each material boundary, including access, data, functionality, tool/action and output use.
Bypass, fallback and administrative paths are included.
limitations: Design diagrams or code fragments do not prove deployed enforcement.

capabilityEvidence.title: Purpose-aligned evaluation results
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Evaluation demonstrates performance, misuse resistance and boundary behavior in representative intended and foreseeable-use conditions.
acceptanceConditions: Test scope traces to the declared purpose, prohibited uses, affected persons and operating conditions.
Results identify system version, data, thresholds, failures and unresolved limitations.
limitations: A test plan or synthetic demo without executed results cannot establish TESTED assurance.

capabilityEvidence.title: Operational use and drift records
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Current operating evidence shows actual use remains within the declared boundary and material drift is detected.
acceptanceConditions: Telemetry, review records or case samples cover actual users, use cases, outputs, escalations and prohibited-use signals.
The observation period and coverage are representative for the assessed operation.
limitations: Absence of reported incidents does not prove boundary conformance.

capabilityEvidence.title: Material-change and requalification record
capabilityEvidence.claimSupported: Scope expansion, new users, functions, data, integrations or effects trigger documented requalification before continued use.
acceptanceConditions: Decision record identifies the change, impact on intended purpose, required reassessment and authorization outcome.
Unapproved expansion is prevented or constrained pending decision.
limitations: A backlog item or informal acknowledgement is not authorization.

antipatternEvidence.title: Purpose statement corpus and inconsistency analysis
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: The system purpose is vague, technically framed, conflicting or materially incomplete.
acceptanceConditions: Collects current authoritative purpose statements across registration, product, contract, design and operational records.
Identifies contradictions, undefined terms and missing decision context.
limitations: A wording difference is not a finding unless it changes material scope or authority.

antipatternEvidence.title: Reachable-use and audience comparison
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: Reachable users, functions or effects exceed the declared purpose or omit affected-person boundaries.
acceptanceConditions: Compares interfaces, access, features, integrations and workflows with declared users and uses.
Includes administrative, fallback and indirect-use paths.
limitations: A technically possible but inaccessible function is not automatically reachable use.

antipatternEvidence.title: Permitted/prohibited-use enforceability test
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: Declared boundaries are too generic or unenforced to distinguish allowed, disallowed and misuse conditions.
acceptanceConditions: Executes representative boundary and misuse cases.
Records expected and actual control behavior for the current system version.
limitations: A policy review without executed tests cannot establish tested absence.

antipatternEvidence.title: Purpose-change and scope-expansion history
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: Prototype, feature, audience, data or decision scope expanded without requalification.
acceptanceConditions: Traces material changes to impact analysis, reassessment and authorization records.
Identifies continued use before or without the required decision.
limitations: Normal maintenance inside an already approved boundary is not scope expansion.

antipatternEvidence.title: Affected-person and downstream-impact review
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: Material affected persons or downstream uses are absent from the purpose boundary.
acceptanceConditions: Uses accountable domain, legal, risk and affected-person expertise.
Records exclusions and uncertainties explicitly.
limitations: A generic impact assessment not tied to the assessed system cannot resolve this claim.

antipatternEvidence.title: Scoped absence-test package
antipatternEvidence.claimSupported: A current, executed and independently reviewed test covers all material AP-A1 failure mechanisms.
acceptanceConditions: Covers vague purpose, conflicting statements, missing users/affected persons, unenforced use boundaries and unauthorized scope expansion.
Identifies system version, scope, test cases, results, residual limitations and independent reviewer.
limitations: Silence, missing incidents, document presence or unsuccessful discovery is never TESTED_ABSENT.

evidenceCeilings: Purpose documentation can establish DECLARED intent but not implemented control or operational conformance.
Implementation or configuration evidence can establish boundary controls but not their effectiveness in representative use.
Executed evaluation can establish TESTED assurance only for the assessed version, scope and conditions.
Operational records can establish OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED assurance only for covered users, functions, time periods and environments.
falsePositiveGuards: Do not treat a product name, model card or marketing description as a system-specific purpose statement.
Do not treat access restriction alone as evidence that permitted and prohibited uses are defined.
Do not treat high model accuracy as evidence that downstream use and decision authority are appropriate.
Do not treat a generic acceptable-use policy as proof of system-specific enforcement.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer affected-person coverage from a list of direct users.
Do not infer implementation from policy approval.
Do not infer operational conformance from missing complaints, incidents or prohibited-use detections.
Do not infer authorization for a new use from technical capability or prototype availability.
Do not infer legal compliance from satisfaction of this capability.
contradictionHandling: Conflicting purpose statements, interfaces, contracts, telemetry or stakeholder accounts keep the affected conclusion UNKNOWN until resolved.
Where implementation enables a broader use than the approved statement, assess the broader reachable use and record the divergence.
A more recent approved record supersedes older intent only when system identity, scope and change authority are explicit.
freshnessRules: Purpose and boundary evidence must match the assessed system and release version.
Operational evidence must be recent enough to represent the current model, workflow, user population and integrations.
Material changes invalidate prior boundary assurance until impact review and targeted reassessment are complete.

evidenceCeilings: Document inconsistency can establish a declaration gap but not the complete reachable-use surface.
Implementation comparison can establish reachable divergence but not frequency or operational consequence.
Operational history can establish observed scope expansion only for covered periods and change records.
TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete absence-test contract; no lower assurance state can be interpreted as absence.
falsePositiveGuards: Do not treat concise wording as vague when the controlled definitions and linked boundaries are precise.
Do not treat a general-purpose model as an undefined-purpose system when the deployed use is system-specifically bounded.
Do not treat every feature change as scope expansion; test whether users, decisions, data, effects or risk materially changed.
Do not infer a missing affected-person boundary solely from absence of direct end users.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer absence from no reported misuse, no complaint, no incident or no detected contradiction.
Do not infer an approved scope change from release, backlog, technical enablement or stakeholder demand.
Do not infer legal non-compliance solely from AP-A1 presence.
Do not infer a broad purpose is acceptable because the underlying model is marketed as general-purpose.
contradictionHandling: Conflicting authoritative statements establish at least UNKNOWN and may support presence when the conflict changes material scope.
Where declared and reachable use conflict, preserve both evidence paths and assess the broader reachable boundary.
Human adjudication is required where business, legal and technical authorities disagree about the operative purpose.
freshnessRules: Use the current production, pilot or evaluation version and current authoritative statements.
Repeat absence testing after any material change.
Operational and change records must cover the period in which the alleged expansion could have occurred.

requiredArtifacts: Independent review record and residual limitation statement
apAbsenceContract.interpretationBoundary: Authoritative purpose-statement corpus and reconciliation; Reachable-use and audience comparison; Executed permitted/prohibited/misuse boundary test results; Material-change and scope-expansion trace; Independent review record and residual limitation statement
